observatoryHome.title: Understand the recommendation, not just the output.
observatoryHome.subtitle: Observatory is the inspection surface for QDIP decisions. Every application follows the same narrative: recommendation first, then alternatives, evidence and trace.
observatoryHome.confidence: Generated from the configured scenario and operational constraints
alternativeItems: Responsible person changes the proposed plan
observatoryHome.traceBody: Needs and available teams → feasible allocations → constraint checks → priority evaluation → recommended allocation.
observatoryHome.demosBody: Different domains, the same inspection grammar. Open an application to examine a real recommendation and the evidence behind it.
observatoryHome.inspect: The four questions Observatory should answer
questions: See the selected action and viable alternatives.
Inspect evidence, priorities, constraints and trade-offs.
Compare the state and scenario that produced a different result.
Explore which constraints or evidence can move the recommendation.
observatoryHome.note: Demos are preconfigured decision applications. Studio configures the decision model; QDIP Core evaluates it; Observatory makes the result inspectable.

decisionChallenge.title: Make the decision before QDIP does
decisionChallenge.intro: Allocate the same constrained resources QDIP will receive. Your choice is locked before the recommendation is calculated.
decisionChallenge.howIntro: You control 4 teams that must be assigned across 5 competing locations.
decisionChallenge.howGoal: Goal: make the best allocation you can using each location’s demand, team skills and capacity, the budget and hard constraints.
howSteps: Review the teams and the demand at each location.
In “Your decision”, choose one allowed location for each team.
Select “Check constraints”. If the allocation is infeasible, adjust it and check again.
When the allocation is feasible, lock your decision. You cannot change it in this run.
QDIP then solves the exact same frozen problem without seeing or changing your choice.
Compare your allocation with QDIP by modeled economic value and inspect the explanation.
decisionChallenge.howImportant: QDIP’s recommendation stays hidden until you lock your own decision.
decisionChallenge.ownDataHelp: Upload aggregated Resource Allocation data (CSV / XML / XLSX). The file is validated before a new frozen challenge is created.
decisionChallenge.scenarioDescription: Allocate constrained teams across five competing locations before seeing the QDIP recommendation.
decisionChallenge.evaluating: QDIP is evaluating the same problem…
decisionChallenge.feasible: Your allocation satisfies the hard constraints.
decisionChallenge.locked: Decision locked. It cannot be changed for this run.
decisionChallenge.noExpected: Expected value and probability risk are not shown because this challenge has no probability model.
decisionChallenge.ctaTitle: Test the same decision pattern on your data
decisionChallenge.ctaText: This was a simulated decision. QDIP can evaluate the same type of decision using your real constraints, costs and operational data.
decisionChallenge.tie: Both decisions have the same modeled value.
decisionChallenge.humanBetter: Your decision has the higher modeled value.
decisionChallenge.qdipBetter: QDIP has the higher modeled value.

onboarding.title: Tell GTM Lab what you sell
onboarding.description: QDIP needs your commercial context before it can judge whether a company is relevant to you. This context is sent to the decision engine; the browser does not calculate prospect scores.
onboarding.offeringPlaceholder: e.g. Decision support software for operational resource allocation
onboarding.problemsPlaceholder: e.g. manual capacity allocation, staff scheduling, planning under constraints
onboarding.contextRequired: Describe your offer and at least one problem it solves before evaluating prospects.
onboarding.howDescription: The backend combines your declared commercial context with evidence supplied for each company. Missing information increases uncertainty instead of being invented.
onboarding.metricOpportunityDescription: How strongly the available evidence supports a meaningful decision problem.
onboarding.metricUncertaintyDescription: How much important information is still unresolved.
onboarding.metricEvidenceDescription: Quality and relevance of the evidence behind the decision.
onboarding.metricConfidenceDescription: Confidence after accounting for uncertainty and evidence quality.
onboarding.metricFitDescription: How well the identified problem matches the declared offer / available capability.
onboarding.demoTitle: See the product before using your data
onboarding.demoDescription: Open a deterministic example portfolio to understand CONTACT / RESEARCH / WATCH / SKIP, evidence, uncertainty and next actions.
onboarding.csvDescription: CSV contains facts you already know about candidate companies. Only name is required; richer descriptions produce more grounded evaluations.
onboarding.templateColumns: Columns: name, domain, country, industry, employee_count, revenue_eur, description. Required: name.

import.tooManyRows: Public evaluation supports at most 10 companies per run.
import.validationFailed: The CSV could not be validated.
import.importFailed: The CSV could not be imported.
import.evaluationFailed: The companies could not be evaluated.

workspace.title: Mobile team allocation plan
workspace.capacity: Available capacity versus the baseline plan
workspace.unavailableTeamHint: See how the plan changes if one team cannot work during this horizon.
workspace.emptyText: QDIP accounts for needs, team skills, current locations, location availability and movement across the full planning horizon.
workspace.valueProp: QDIP helps decide where to send mobile teams so more priority needs are covered with the resources already available.
workspace.heroQuestion: Can the same teams cover more priority demand?
workspace.differentiation: Unlike a spreadsheet, QDIP evaluates consequences across the full horizon: where a team ends today changes what is feasible tomorrow.
workspace.whyTitle: Review the recommendation logic before deciding
workspace.baselineCapacityHint: 100% is the currently planned availability; lower or higher values simulate changed conditions.
workspace.unavailableHint: Simulate a location that mobile teams temporarily cannot serve.
workspace.heuristic: Large decision spaces use deterministic branch-aware beam search; the interface does not present a heuristic result as a mathematically guaranteed global optimum.

importer.title: Client data
importer.body: Upload aggregated operational data only. Do not include beneficiary names, phones, addresses or other personal data.
importer.drop: Drag and drop a file here
importer.templateIntro: The CSV contains several row types. The record_type field determines what each row describes. Fill only the columns relevant to that record type; the remaining columns may stay empty.

recordTypes.settings: global planning settings: budget, target coverage and planning unit
recordTypes.community: a location and its persistent constraints
recordTypes.community_day: location availability and constraints for a specific day
recordTypes.demand: service demand for a location and day
recordTypes.team: a team, its skills, capacity and allowed locations
recordTypes.team_day: team availability or capacity for a specific day
recordTypes.travel: travel cost and time between two locations
recordTypes.baseline: manual plan used for comparison with the QDIP recommendation

importer.multiValueHint: For fields with multiple values, such as skills, days or allowed_communities, separate values with |.
importer.starterBody: Download the minimal template or a complete fictional example, edit it in Excel / Google Sheets, then upload it back here.
